results.claim: Under the muṣḥaf-spiral placement, āyāt sharing a rare root lie closer in direction than random pairs — including across sūrahs — while the legacy برج placement shows no such locality.
results.null: one endpoint replaced by a uniformly random āyah (200 seeded draws); legacy: random legacy node
results.note: Locality under muṣḥaf order is partly by construction: rare roots recur inside one story. The cross-sūrah figure is the part that is not.

results.claim: Lexical continuity across an isnād seam (the stitch half of رِباط = √(continuity × delta)) exceeds the continuity across an arbitrary non-seam point in the same sūrah.
results.null: paired control: a uniformly drawn non-seam word index (±2 excluded) in the same sūrah, same ±8-word windows
results.note: If refused, the continuity half of the master metric is a property of the text's vocabulary at that scale, not of seams; the metric then ranks seams by delta with a lexical gate, and should be read that way.

results.claim: The last three āyāt of a sūrah sit nearer to direct address (lower discourse distance) than the sūrah's own average.
results.null: three āyāt drawn at random within the same sūrah (2,000 seeded draws); sūrahs with ≥12 āyāt
results.note: A shift is a shift in the engine's person tagging, not a claim about the closing of sūrahs as such.

results.claim: A seeded voyage (evidence-weighted, with memory) visits more distinct sūrahs and revisits fewer āyāt in 40 legs than a uniform random walk over the same relations.
results.null: uniform random neighbour walk from the same start (no weights, no memory); also a muṣḥaf-order-only walk
results.note: An interaction claim: the voyage is worth its parameters only if it shows more of the text per minute than chance.

results.claim: At this field's scale, the floating origin is needed to keep vertex quantisation below visibility.
results.null: absolute float32 coordinates with no rebasing
results.note: Absolute float32 error at the field's scale is 7.3e-4 px at the closest viewing distance. Whatever the verdict, the floating origin is insurance for free flight far outside the field, which nothing prevents.

results.claim: Āyāt with no person mass are not spread evenly over the muṣḥaf; they concentrate in particular sūrahs beyond what sūrah length explains.
results.null: each sūrah receives unattributed āyāt in proportion to its āyah count (χ², df = 113)
results.note: Descriptive of the tagging, not of the text: an āyah has no person mass when no segment the engine reads as attribution carries a person.
